sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Sergio Martínez-Beltrán
articles.description: The person shot is in serious but stable condition, Austin Mayor Kirk Watson said in a press conference.
articles.title: Federal immigration agent shoots and injures man in Austin, Texas

articles.author: Kristin Wright
articles.description: The lions were found dead inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a popular wildlife reserve in Tanzania. Deaths raise concerns over wildlife poisonings in East Africa.
articles.title: Poison suspected in deaths of ten lions in game reserve in Tanzania

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has faced a major electoral setback in two state elections, with his center-right party losing ground. The far-right Alternative for Germany party made significant gains.
articles.title: Germany's Merz vows to press ahead with reforms after historic state election defeat

articles.author: Kristin Wright
articles.description: President Trump has claimed that military operations are needed at his proposed triumphal arch in Washington D.C., in order to protect national security. A federal court is weighing the arch's legality.
articles.title: Trump says his D.C. arch will serve as 'military complex' with snipers and drones

articles.author: Kamala Thiagarajan
articles.description: In the bustling heart of the southern Indian city of Chennai is a market that never sleeps, where residents from the poorest neighborhoods wage a battle of survival with the sea.
articles.title: PHOTOS: The precarious life of fisherfolk

articles.author: Debbie Elliott
articles.description: At Bayou Bar, music and food go hand in hand.  Which is why a new cookbook from chef Brian Landry and bandleader Peter Harris has recipes from the menu and stories from the musicians who play there.
articles.title: A new cookbook pays tribute to two New Orleans staples — 'Rhythm & Roux'

articles.author: Debbie Elliott
articles.description: In the Lower Ninth Ward, an old Family Dollar stands covered in graffiti. It looks abandoned. But inside, it's a treasure trove — clothing, home goods, toys and books. And everything is free.
articles.title: In New Orleans, an empty building becomes a free store — and roller skating rink

articles.author: Maddy Lauria
articles.description: Fox Corp. must turn over hundreds of documents that could shed light on how founder Rupert Murdoch handled some of his media companies' biggest scandals.
articles.title: Judge orders Fox to hand over hundreds of documents in shareholders' case

articles.author: Joe Hernandez
articles.description: Grandparents taking care of their grandkids is nothing new. But the surging cost of childcare in the U.S. has made familial support even more critical for some parents who struggle to afford it.
articles.title: U.S. childcare costs are astronomical. More families are turning to grandparents

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.
articles.title: Ukraine fires over 1,000 drones at Russia, including hundreds launched at Moscow

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Dan Tehan says fuel excise cut when oil price high a ‘sensible’ plan
Dan Tehan, the shadow minister for energy, said Gallagher’s criticism of the Coalition’s fuel plan wasn’t fair.
[What] I would say to Anthony Albanese and the Labor party is get out amongst the people and see what’s happening in your electorates because people are hurting because of cost of living …
We have the discipline to be able to do the policy work to make sure we can offset policies like this so it won’t be inflationary and it will provide much needed relief to people, and they need it now.
Obviously we’ve helped when the war started with some changes to the fuel excise but we’ve shifted, and [are] including in the budget, to providing more permanent cost of living arrangements, including through the tax system, to make sure that that ongoing cost-of-living help is there permanently, not just in these one-off arrangements, which, when we’ve got higher inflation, could be difficult in the economy.
Our decisions have been built and baked into the budget to make sure that that cost-of-living help is permanent. You know, the sooner this war in the Middle East stops, the better.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: Wong speaks to Palestinian foreign minister about Gaza; Queensland premier says plans to reduce visas are ‘nuts’

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
The 31-year-old former police officer has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder as his trial begins in Sydney’s supreme court

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former police officer allegedly developed an “infatuation and obsession” with one of his victims, and disguised himself as an Uber Eats rider before shooting two men, a court has heard.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter as his trial began in Sydney’s supreme court on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NSW cop Beau Lamarre-Condon disguised himself as Uber Eats rider before alleged murders, court hears

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Government warned ‘skills revolution’ at risk amid slow start to project with target of 30,000 starts by end of parliament
Labour has been warned its “skills revolution” to tackle youth unemployment risks failure, after its flagship apprenticeship scheme enrolled only 160 young people in its first eight months.
The shortfall, highlighted in a report by the Fabian Society, leaves the government well off track of achieving its ambition of 30,000 “foundation apprenticeship” starts by the end of this parliament.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Only 160 apprenticeship starts in eight months on Labour’s flagship scheme

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff in Jersey
articles.description:
While global billionaires and multinational companies have been lured to its shores, many islanders feel left behind and priced out, with food bank use increasing
On a late Friday afternoon on the Channel Island of Jersey, tourists and locals are flocking to St Helier’s waterfront where the town’s sprawling beach has emerged at low tide.
In one direction, they face the calm waters of St Aubin’s Bay, ringed by a seaside promenade and punctuated with a tidal island hosting the 16th century Elizabeth Castle.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s unrecognisable’: How being a tax haven has changed Jersey

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Unions, thinktanks and others say overhaul could provide investment Britain needs
Unions, thinktanks, environmental groups and charities have come together to call on ministers to boost the financial firepower of the national wealth fund to empower it to invest more in Britain and rebalance the country’s economy.
Lower energy bills, the revitalisation of the UK’s industrial heartlands and the provision of more high-quality jobs could all be unlocked by scaling up the NWF, according to a statement from organisations including the TUC, Greenpeace, WWF and the New Economics Foundation.
Turbocharging the retrofitting of homes and buildings.
Giving the public a bigger stake in critical infrastructure through taking part-ownership stakes in key projects.
Launching a targeted investment programme to bring new green industries to communities hit hardest by deindustrialisation.
Supporting a network of regional banks to funnel money into the small businesses that hold up local economies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK urged to strengthen financial muscle of national wealth fund to aid economy

articles.author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
articles.description:
Seventh intergenerational report also outlines how Australia is at cusp of an uncertain age of artificial intelligence

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

There will be more Australians dying than being born in 40 years’ time, according to the government’s latest intergenerational report, which lays bare the fundamental challenges of managing an ageing population at a time of rapid change and lower economic growth.
The country’s seventh IGR also outlines how Australia is at the cusp of a new and uncertain age of artificial intelligence that will shape the economy and society over the coming four decades.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More Australians will be dying than being born in 40 years as major report predicts future of lower growth

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos
articles.description:
In a 60 Minutes interview, ex-husband describes moments leading to the 2023 killings
In his first televised interview, Patrick Clancy, the ex-husband of Lindsay Clancy, described the moments leading up to the 2023 killings of their children and how he coped in the aftermath.
Patrick Clancy responded to online criticism and conspiracy theories from people who supported Lindsay Clancy and believed he did not provide enough care to his wife at the time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Patrick Clancy, ex-husband of Lindsay Clancy, opens up on children’s killings in first televised interview

articles.author: Ima Caldwell and AAP
articles.description:
Bystanders found all four on the side of the road at Valley Heights on Sunday with stabbing injuries

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Police have alleged that a mother was behind a stabbing attack on three young children that left one dead and two others fighting for their lives in hospital.
The woman, aged in her 40s, is also in a critical condition.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police allege mother stabbed three children in Blue Mountains leaving one child dead

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy
articles.description:
Though the man of the hour is unable to attend, fans flock to Rod Laver Arena and cinemas nationwide to celebrate the songs of an Australian icon
At a Sydney shopping centre on a balmy Sunday evening, hundreds of people gathered to watch a concert that, according to its host, Richard Wilkins, would set a new livestreaming record for Australian cinemas.
Experiencing a Rod Laver Arena event with popcorn in a cinema chair was unusual in itself – but so too was the fact that its hero, John Farnham, would not be performing, or even in attendance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: John Farnham tribute: Céline Dion, Chris Martin and Hugh Jackman honour ‘living legend’ at livestreamed concert

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Two leaders meet in French territory off Canada as Ottawa seeks stronger relations with EU while fighting trade war with US
The leaders of France and Canada have pledged closer ties to grapple with rising geopolitical tensions, climate change and the erosion of democratic values, after ⁠they met in a ⁠French territory off Canada’s Atlantic coast.
The two leaders’ visit to Saint-Pierre ​and Miquelon – the first by a French president since 2014 and the first by a Canadian prime minister – came just weeks ⁠after Donald Trump posted an image showing the islands, as well as all of Canada and other countries in North America, covered by the US flag.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Macron and Carney announce closer France-Canada ties amid Trump tensions

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Anti-ICE protests break out in push for transparency as unnamed man is in serious but stable condition at hospital
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon in Texas’s capital of Austin, local authorities said, and anti-ICE protesters quickly gathered at the scene.
The unnamed man was in serious but stable condition at a hospital after being shot once in the torso on the city’s north side, Austin’s police chief, Lisa Davis, said at a news conference with the mayor and other city officials.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICE agent shoots and wounds man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas, officials say

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos
articles.description:
President’s latest order expected to bring NIH funding under control of Trump administration to align with agenda
Donald Trump’s latest executive order is expected to establish a board responsible for approving National Institutes of Health grant funding, marking another attempt by the Trump administration to censor topics that do not align with the president’s agenda.
The executive order, reported by outlets including the Washington Post and Politico, was discussed in a meeting on Friday where senior administration officials accused the NIH of funding “woke” initiatives that went against Trump’s political priorities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump reportedly to form health funding board that could veto ‘woke’ initiatives

articles.author: Peter Walker and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
Proposal one of many at conference responding to concern voters unaware of party’s policies or what it stands for
The Liberal Democrats say they will tax big tech to finance a new online crime agency, as they try to address concerns that not enough voters know what the party stands for.
The plan, to be announced at the party conference on Monday by the Lib Dems’ home affairs spokesperson, Max Wilkinson, would create a new Online Crime Agency focused on offences including child sexual abuse material, trafficking in drugs and weapons, and deepfake AI-generated pornographic images.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lib Dems propose big tech levy to fund £250m online crime agency

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Funding boost for facilities and fixed dates for trials designed to encourage more survivors to come forward
Specialist courtrooms prioritising cases of rape and other serious sex offences are to be introduced across England and Wales, with campaigners welcoming the move as potentially transformative.
The changes, designed to encourage more survivors to come forward, will include the provision of private entrances and waiting rooms, and facilities equipped for recording evidence in advance and observing sentencing remotely.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Specialist courtrooms to prioritise rape cases in England and Wales

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Jovenel Moïse, 53, was shot dead in July 2021 in a killing which sparked chaos in Haiti
Eighteen people have been arrested in association with the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, according to US officials.
Moïse, 53, was shot dead on 7 July 2021 at his private residence by a hired group of about 20 military-trained Colombian mercenaries. His security detail did not intervene to protect him.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More than a dozen arrested in connection with 2021 assassination of Haitian president

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Bridget Phillipson says Burnham’s past criticisms of US president not an issue as PM prepares to meet Trump at UN
Next month’s budget will be made more difficult by Donald Trump’s war with Iran, one of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said, while adding she did not expect the prime minister’s previous disparaging comments about the US president to be an issue.
Burnham is expected to meet Trump early next week at the UN general assembly summit in New York, the pair having previously spoken twice by phone since Burnham entered No 10.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK minister warns of impact of Trump’s Iran war on next month’s budget

articles.author: Patrick Wintour in New York
articles.description:
Tensions grow as Trump tells Fox News he is considering ‘wiping Iran out’ after attacks on Riyadh by Houthi rebels
Governments across the Middle East are bracing for an escalation of violence after Iran claimed it had received intelligence that the US was preparing for a renewed bombing campaign against the Islamic Republic.
In a potential sign of growing tensions before the UN general assembly in New York this week, Donald Trump cut short a weekend visit to the Camp David presidential retreat on Sunday with no official explanation, and a new security alert was issued by the state department to all US citizens in the Middle East.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East braces for more violence as Iran claims US is planning to renew bombing campaign

articles.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
articles.description:
Far-right AfD wins in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and leftwing Die Linke on course for victory in Berlin
Germany’s embattled chancellor, Friedrich Merz, has vowed to stay in office and fight for future-proofing economic changes despite heavy losses for his conservatives in two state elections, one to the far right and the other to a leftwing party.
Preliminary results indicated Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU) tallied just 4.9%, below ⁠the 5% threshold needed to enter the state parliament and indicating they may be excluded altogether. It would be the CDU’s worst-ever state score, which Merz called a “disaster”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Friedrich Merz vows to stay in office after CDU ‘disaster’ in German state elections

articles.author: Helena Smith in Athens
articles.description:
Row at Athenian riviera resort turned violent after two elderly bathers reportedly argued over shortage of loungers
Greek police are investigating the death of an 82-year-old man after a brawl over a sunlounger at a beach on the Athenian riviera.
The man had arrived at the popular bathing spot of Vouliagmeni before 10am on Sunday hoping to secure a sunbed, but he soon began arguing with a fellow bather – described by authorities as a “76-year-old man unknown to him” – when it became clear loungers were in short supply.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man, 82, dies after brawl with 76-year-old over sunlounger on Greek beach

articles.author: Ed Pilkington
articles.description:
Florida’s María Elvira Salazar warns Trump that advisers are ‘compromising his legacy’ and not showing ‘whole picture’
María Elvira Salazar, the Republican congresswoman who has accused the president of going too far on immigration enforcement, doubled down on her criticism of the administration on Sunday, warning Donald Trump that some of his advisers were “compromising his legacy”.
In an interview with CBS News’s Face the Nation, the Florida representative who is locked in a tight race for re-election pleaded with the US president not to “squander” his relationship with Hispanic voters. Though she couched her remarks as criticism of top administration advisers, it was clear that her focus was on Trump’s much-vaunted ambition to carry out the largest mass deportation of undocumented immigrants in US history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House Republican doubles down on jab at Trump’s immigration enforcement

articles.author: Shaun Walker in Prague and Riga
articles.description:
Exclusive: Intelligence officers say Russian campaign could intensify ‘in months, not years’ – but that panic risks playing into Kremlin psy-ops
European intelligence officials have raised the possibility of an imminent Russian test of Nato, with one saying a potential attack could come in a matter of “months, not years”.
The warnings come after Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, told parliament that intelligence assessments suggested Russia might launch an attack with drones or missiles on Nato territory in the coming months, as part of efforts to prove that “article 5 is more theoretical than practical”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: European spy chiefs warn Moscow is planning more decisive action against Nato

articles.author: Benjamin Lee
articles.description:
The queer period drama wins Oscar-predicting award, being named the most popular audience film at the festival
The Spanish queer drama La Bola Negra has won this year’s people’s choice award at the Toronto film festival.
The film, which takes place in 1932, 1937 and 2017, focuses on the lives of interconnected gay men. It premiered at this year’s Cannes film festival with the Guardian’s Peter Bradshaw calling it “handsomely produced, lovingly detailed and confidently constructed” in a four-star review.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: La Bola Negra wins Toronto film festival people’s choice award

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh, Pjotr Sauer and agencies
articles.description:
At least three people killed and oil refinery damaged as doubts cast over initial reports of ballistic missile use
Ukraine has targeted Moscow and the surrounding region in a large-scale attack that involved hundreds of drones.
The attack killed at least three people and damaged what Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said was one of Russia’s “key oil industry facilities” on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections, authorities said on Sunday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine targets Moscow with hundreds of drones on final day of Russian election

articles.author: Reuters in Geneva
articles.description:
Former president of Chile drops out after support collapsed in security council straw poll, leaving seven candidates in contest
Michelle Bachelet, a former president of Chile, has withdrawn her candidacy to become the next secretary general of the ⁠UN, ending an attempt ​that had struggled to gain traction among security council members.
Bachelet, 74, announced ⁠her decision in a video posted on Instagram on Saturday, saying: “I will now continue, with the ⁠same determination as always, my international work.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michelle Bachelet withdraws from race to become UN secretary general

articles.author: Rebecca Bailey China correspondent
articles.description:
Beijing believes slowdown calls aim to lock in US advantage, and is pursuing a different balance between safety and pace

China bogeyman looms large over American firms’ AI doomsday scenario

About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it.
His clients, well-off parents looking to send their children to study overseas, had begun arriving in his office reeling off information and opinions gleaned not from rival firms, but from chatbots.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development

articles.author: Donna Ferguson, Yassin El-Moudden and agencies
articles.description:
Authorities issued warnings for city in first such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July
Yemen’s Houthis said they attacked “sensitive” sites in the Saudi capital with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport on Saturday.
The Saudi government sent air raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks, marking the first time the government has issued such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport as Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital

articles.author: Associated Press in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Elor Azaria’s conviction in 2017 for manslaughter of man who stabbed soldier continues to divide country
Israel’s president has pardoned a combat medic who shot dead a badly wounded Palestinian attacker who had stabbed a soldier in the occupied West Bank, in a case that divided the country a decade ago.
Elor Azaria’s conviction in 2017 for manslaughter and his release after serving two-thirds of his 18-month sentence drew enormous attention in Israel, where military service is compulsory for most Jewish men.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli president pardons combat medic who shot dead wounded Palestinian attacker

articles.author: Peter Beaumont
articles.description:
As Gaza documentary wins cinematic acclaim, its directors face vitriol in Israel amid a febrile election campaign
First there was a moment of stunned silence. Then, in the Sala Grande, the main screening hall of the Venice film festival within the Palazzo del Cinema, the audience stood almost as one and turned to applaud the film-makers for 25 minutes.
The film the audience had watched for 80 harrowing minutes was the Gaza documentary NAZA, which has been produced by the Guardian.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From ovations in Venice to death threats in Israel: the extreme responses to NAZA documentary

articles.author: Maanvi Singh
articles.description:
Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence

Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.
The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan and agencies
articles.description:
Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children
Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.
The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Critics say moves from leftwing incumbent president are electorally motivated two weeks before Brazil’s elections
Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced a 15% increase in the country’s main cash-transfer programme for poor families, as well as free weight-loss jabs, prompting criticism from opponents who say the moves are electorally motivated just two weeks before the presidential election.
On 4 October, the leftwing incumbent will face the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who has been gaining ground in recent weeks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Rout raises questions about coordination and morale as some politicians claim billions of dollars were offered to persuade forces to abandon position
A bitter inquest is under way among Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces as to how what was being billed as a decisive assault on Sana’a, the Houthi-controlled capital, suddenly collapsed into a military rout.
More than 15 brigades were defeated as the country’s entire west coast fell into Houthi hands. Efforts are now being made to reorganise the anti-Houthi forces representing the UN-recognised Yemeni government in order to capture the Kahbob mountains, a strategic point from which to restrict Houthi forces moving closer to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces launch inquest into sudden military collapse

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences
Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.
Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Four of Nurat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week
A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed.
Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had offered a reward of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout

articles.author: Agence France-Presse and Associated Press
articles.description:
Simon Peter Carman appeared in a Pattaya court on Friday charged with killing  Tunchanok Donhomla 
An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.
Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian man accused of murdering Thai teenager and putting body in suitcase pleads not guilty

articles.author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
articles.description:
The African serval, illegally enclosed in the back yard, was subdued and transferred to an animal welfare facility 
Louisiana firefighters responding to a small house blaze found a wildcat native to sub-Saharan Africa illegally enclosed in the back yard, prompting an animal welfare agency to seek placing the creature in an appropriate environment, according to officials.
Firefighters investigating a report of a minor fire at a home in the suburban New Orleans community of Marrero on Tuesday spotted the cat in question – an African serval – behind the residence in a chain-linked enclosure resembling a cramped baseball batting cage, a spokesperson for the local animal protection services said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Louisiana firefighters find feline native to sub-Saharan Africa while responding to house fire

articles.author: James Michelin for MetDesk
articles.description:
At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia 
Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.
Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon

articles.author: Ella Creamer
articles.description:
More than 180 writers sign letter renewing calls for information on 12 authors detained incommunicado since 2001 crackdown on free speech by Isaias Afwerki
More than 180 writers have signed a letter to Eritrean president Isaias Afwerki calling for proof of life for 12 writers arrested in 2001.
Nobel laureates Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee join prominent writers including Colm Tóibín, Elif Shafak, Isabel Allende, Ben Okri, Yann Martel, Kamila Shamsie and Tsitsi Dangarembga in signing the letter organised by PEN International and dated 18 September, marking 25 years since a government crackdown on the independent press. “Within days, Eritrea’s free press and the nation’s independent voices were systematically crushed,” opens the letter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We demand the truth’: Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee lead calls for proof of life of disappeared Eritrean writers

articles.author: Mark Sweney and agencies
articles.description:
Increase from 1% to 1.25% follows US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank tightening monetary policy

Business live – latest updates

Japan’s central bank has increased interest rates to a fresh 31-year high as it attempts to combat global inflation linked to the war in Iran.
The Bank of Japan (BoJ) voted to raise its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high to curb impact of rising prices

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Seoul resolves recent speculation over sending military to strait of Hormuz, saying ‘there won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war’
South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, has said he will ⁠not deploy the military to the ⁠Middle East in a way ​that could draw the country into conflict, resisting calls from Donald Trump to support his war in Iran.
“There won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war. I can tell you that very clearly,” Lee said at a ⁠news conference on Friday. “We won’t deploy military assets in any form to that end.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea will not send military to support US war on Iran, defying Trump pressure

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat
A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century.
The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was convicted of aiding the terrorist group that took credit for the suicide bombing 
An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country.
A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IS member sentenced to 20 years in prison for role in 2021 Kabul airport bombing

articles.author: Damien Gayle
articles.description:
Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August
Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found.
Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse, which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi and Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
articles.description:
Kasim and Sulaiman Khan tell Guardian they believe ex-PM is being ‘slowly killed’ by harsh treatment, driven by Asim Munir
The sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions.
Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, have become strong advocates for the release of their father, who has been held in Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023, and is serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Imran Khan’s sons accuse Pakistani army chief of vendetta against imprisoned father

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
After a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi, focus is on how urban areas can adapt to growing populations. Plus, Ahmedabad’s ace newspaper delivery driver goes viral
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Recently, I may have saved a woman’s life on the road. Somehow, this was something I had expected to happen.
On that day, I saw a truck leave a construction site with a tangled wire trailing behind. I frantically looked to see what the wire was attached to and spotted the scaffolding a few meters ahead. I shrieked and grabbed the hand of the woman walking in front of me just as the metal pipes came crashing down. We hugged for a brief second, and then walked our separate ways.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What would it take to make India’s cities better – and safer?

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
While world leaders prepare for annual UN gathering, shifts in the global order continue in the face of a disruptive American president
In the event of a midterms election battering, it is possible that a deflated Donald Trump, constrained by a Democrat-controlled Congress, will gradually have to face up to the indignity of irrelevance.
While continuing to sign off Truth Social posts with his usual, “Thank you for your attention to this matter”, no one will actually be paying much attention. His meandering press conferences will no longer be carried live by TV networks. The Republican party will move on to the question of his successor. Trump could announce he had changed the name of the Champs-Élysées to Sunset Boulevard and even Google Maps will stifle a yawn. He would become that most pitied of political animals, the lame duck.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Whiplashed middle powers seek new alliances as Trump rages on world stage

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Anti-ICE protests break out in push for transparency as unnamed man is in serious but stable condition at hospital
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon in Texas’s capital of Austin, local authorities said, and anti-ICE protesters quickly gathered at the scene.
The unnamed man was in serious but stable condition at a hospital after being shot once in the torso on the city’s north side, Austin’s police chief, Lisa Davis, said at a news conference with the mayor and other city officials.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICE agent shoots and wounds man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas, officials say

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos
articles.description:
President’s latest order expected to bring NIH funding under control of Trump administration to align with agenda
Donald Trump’s latest executive order is expected to establish a board responsible for approving National Institutes of Health grant funding, marking another attempt by the Trump administration to censor topics that do not align with the president’s agenda.
The executive order, reported by outlets including the Washington Post and Politico, was discussed in a meeting on Friday where senior administration officials accused the NIH of funding “woke” initiatives that went against Trump’s political priorities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump reportedly to form health funding board that could veto ‘woke’ initiatives

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
PM hopes to be firmer with US leader than his predecessor without provoking diplomatic warfare, as the Iran war weighs on the UK economy
No international relationship has more power to determine the success of Andy Burnham’s premiership. So you might imagine the stakes for the prime minister’s first face-to-face meeting with Donald Trump on Tuesday would be high.

articles.title: Andy Burnham faces a weakened Trump – but the president remains unpredictable

articles.author: Ed Pilkington
articles.description:
Florida’s María Elvira Salazar warns Trump that advisers are ‘compromising his legacy’ and not showing ‘whole picture’
María Elvira Salazar, the Republican congresswoman who has accused the president of going too far on immigration enforcement, doubled down on her criticism of the administration on Sunday, warning Donald Trump that some of his advisers were “compromising his legacy”.
In an interview with CBS News’s Face the Nation, the Florida representative who is locked in a tight race for re-election pleaded with the US president not to “squander” his relationship with Hispanic voters. Though she couched her remarks as criticism of top administration advisers, it was clear that her focus was on Trump’s much-vaunted ambition to carry out the largest mass deportation of undocumented immigrants in US history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House Republican doubles down on jab at Trump’s immigration enforcement

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Candidates have been selected for November’s midterms – have Republicans and Democrats made the right choices?
Primary season has officially concluded in the United States, with Democrats leading the polls among voters amid widespread economic anxieties, a war with Iran and Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda continuing into the end of the year.
Democratic and Republican voters have selected contenders for key races in the 3 November midterms that will decide the balance of power in Congress, and the future of both parties. Democrats have been rocked by the primary victories of leftwing candidates. Republicans have doubled down on backing the president’s policies, despite his low approval ratings. And both parties are navigating the fallout from a series of scandals that have forced some candidates from the race, while others decided to press on.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Leftists make waves and Trump flexes muscles: US primary season takeaways

articles.author: Michael Sainato
articles.description:
Meet the candidates with labor ties vying for Senate and House seats in midterm races. Most of the nominees are Democrats as the party looks to rebuild support among working-class voters
The US labor movement is having a banner election year.
More than three dozen nominees for open House and Senate races across the US have backgrounds as labor union representatives or members.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Revenge of the labor movement: Democrats with union backgrounds aim to retake Congress

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early
articles.description:
Silicon Valley China hawks, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei among them, fear the country surpassing US’s AI lead as much as superintelligence destroying humanity

Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development

When reporters asked Donald Trump this week if he supported calls to slow down the development of artificial intelligence out of growing fears for cybersecurity, public safety and the fate of humanity, he said no. His argument: China.
“We’re leading China in AI,” Trump said. “We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to ⁠keep it that way, because whoever wins AI, wins.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China bogeyman looms large over American firms’ AI doomsday scenario

articles.author: Anna North
articles.description:
Local communities are fighting back against the influence of conservative groups like Moms for Liberty in education
Jimmy Glover’s youngest children were in high school when he noticed their Florida school district taking an unsettling turn. Beloved books were being pulled from shelves. Teachers were scared of being targeted.
“There was this culture of fear that was permeating throughout the district,” Glover said of Sarasota county.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No more book bans: how Florida students are pushing rightwingers out of school boards

articles.author: Jared Abbott and Joan C Williams
articles.description:
The party needs to thread the needle between college-educated and working-class voters. Our survey offers a way
Resisting authoritarianism is the second-highest priority for Democrats’ college-educated base. But for working-class Americans, it’s only the 19th priority (out of 20), we found in a new survey. The gap between these two groups was larger than on any other issues: elites prioritized resisting authoritarianism an astonishing 33 percentage points more than non-elites did.
Democrats’ dilemma is that their college-educated base insists they stand up to Donald Trump’s attacks on democracy, but they also need to win working-class votes. The way to thread that needle is to recognize that what’s needed to defend democracy in the short term is different from what’s needed to defend it in the long term.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: To protect democracy, Democrats should talk about corruption – not authoritarianism | Jared Abbott and Joan C Williams

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with Blake Montgomery , produced by Nada Smiljanic and John Rogers; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Tech bosses have called for a slowdown in artificial intelligence and formal guardrails to be introduced by the US government. But President Trump is not moved by the doomsday predictions, calling them a ‘hoax'. What is behind his affection for the AI industry? Jonathan Freedland and Guardian US tech editor Blake Montgomery discuss
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Trump’s AI obsession walking the world into disaster? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Martin J Riedl and Samuel Woolley
articles.description:
Secret coordination between politicians and social media creators is a form of astroturfing. But there are few legal regulations
Not long ago, it was common wisdom among social media influencers that they shouldn’t talk politics. There was a widespread belief among their crowd that it was bad for business. If you went left, you lost the right, and vice-versa.
Times have changed. Nearly everywhere you look online, influencers are posting political content. Each day, there are new reports detailing their hot takes on elections, campaigns and the culture wars. It’s become a lucrative business for these creators, as they now like to be called, and a boost for those that pay them for hype.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Paid influencers are everywhere in US politics. We need transparency | Martin J Riedl and Samuel Woolley

articles.author: Vince Beiser
articles.description:
Trump himself has acknowledged the US need for Canadian aluminum – and has largely exempted metals from new tariffs
As trade talks with Canada shambled toward collapse in late August, Donald Trump brayed on Truth Social: “WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!” But in fact, Canada, like China, has something the US needs badly: critical metals that undergird modern military technology.
Canada is the United States’s biggest foreign source of minerals, supplying about $47bin worth each year. Sixty per cent of all the aluminum the US uses each year, for instance, comes from Canada, where mighty, remote rivers provide smelting plants vast quantities of cheap, low-carbon electricity. The US military uses the lightweight metal for everything from shell casings to ship hulls and aircraft fuselage. The Pentagon’s cutting-edge F-35 fighter jet’s airframe is about 40% aluminum. “This country desperately needs aluminum,” Trump complained last month. “We get it all from Canada for the most part, and we need it badly.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says the US doesn’t need Canada. But it’s the source of key minerals for the military | Vince Beiser

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
The US decision to remove limits on coal and gas plant emissions is rooted in a perception of manliness in these industries
You can impress a certain kind of person at a party by reciting the fact that there are more yoga instructors in the US than there are coalminers. In fact, the disparity is greater than this catchy phrasing suggests: there are actually more yoga instructors in the US than there are people employed in the entirety of the coalmining industry, miners and otherwise. It’s not even especially close: about 38,000 people in the US work in coal, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, compared to about 100,000 yoga instructors who are registered with the Yoga Alliance, an industry group.
If you looked only at the numbers, you might think a politician would be incentivized to talk about the interests of the yoga industry, about the dignity that yoga jobs give to American families, or about the need to foster growth in the yoga industry, more than they talk about these things for coal; after all, yoga, not coal, is putting food on the table in more American households. But no politician would ever talk about the interests of yoga teachers, or wax poetic about their role in the American dream, the way they do with coal miners; if they did, they’d be laughed out of the room. And we all know why: yoga is thought of as decadent, cosmopolitan and feminine, while coal mining is imagined as hardscrabble, honorable and masculine.
Moira Donegan is a Guardian US columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s love of fossil fuels is about more than money | Moira Donegan

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Johana Bhuiyan . Produced by Tiara Chiaramonte engineered by Ivan Kuraev executive producers Jonathan Menjivar and Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
A former Anthropic researcher’s apocalyptic declaration about artificial intelligence has led to a global panic that the technology might be the end of us all. At an event in Washington today to warn about the dangers of AI, US senator Bernie Sanders said that Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel'. Oddly, Steve Bannon appeared at the same event. But is this response a distraction from the more immediate problems AI is already causing? Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian tech reporter Johana Bhuyian to put this moment in context, and she explains why we should be cynical about industry calls for regulation
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the real AI apocalypse is already here – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.description:
During a Senate committee hearing, FBI director answered questions from Republican senator John Kennedy about the bureau's new policy allowing the hiring of people who have engaged in bestiality
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kash Patel defends changes in FBI hiring policy regarding bestiality – video

articles.description:
Bernie Sanders criticised the advancement of artificial intelligence at the Pro-Human Assembly in Washington on Tuesday, warning that the current type of AI was 'the least capable version of AI that we will ever have'. The independent senator from Vermont was speaking at the conference alongside a number of AI sceptics, including Steve Bannon
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bernie Sanders says Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel’ over AI – video

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Government warned ‘skills revolution’ at risk amid slow start to project with target of 30,000 starts by end of parliament
Labour has been warned its “skills revolution” to tackle youth unemployment risks failure, after its flagship apprenticeship scheme enrolled only 160 young people in its first eight months.
The shortfall, highlighted in a report by the Fabian Society, leaves the government well off track of achieving its ambition of 30,000 “foundation apprenticeship” starts by the end of this parliament.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Only 160 apprenticeship starts in eight months on Labour’s flagship scheme

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Unions, thinktanks and others say overhaul could provide investment Britain needs
Unions, thinktanks, environmental groups and charities have come together to call on ministers to boost the financial firepower of the national wealth fund to empower it to invest more in Britain and rebalance the country’s economy.
Lower energy bills, the revitalisation of the UK’s industrial heartlands and the provision of more high-quality jobs could all be unlocked by scaling up the NWF, according to a statement from organisations including the TUC, Greenpeace, WWF and the New Economics Foundation.
Turbocharging the retrofitting of homes and buildings.
Giving the public a bigger stake in critical infrastructure through taking part-ownership stakes in key projects.
Launching a targeted investment programme to bring new green industries to communities hit hardest by deindustrialisation.
Supporting a network of regional banks to funnel money into the small businesses that hold up local economies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK urged to strengthen financial muscle of national wealth fund to aid economy

articles.author: Richard Adams Education editor
articles.description:
School leaders’ union says new system is worse than one it replaced and has left members  feeling overwhelmed
Headteachers in England want Ofsted to stop grading their schools, saying its new inspection regime is harming their mental health and creating greater stress than the system it was designed to replace.
The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said it has given the education secretary, Lucy Powell, “countless examples” of the damaging effects on its members since the new inspection framework was introduced a year ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Ofsted inspection regime is damaging our health, headteachers say

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff in Jersey
articles.description:
While global billionaires and multinational companies have been lured to its shores, many islanders feel left behind and priced out, with food bank use increasing
On a late Friday afternoon on the Channel Island of Jersey, tourists and locals are flocking to St Helier’s waterfront where the town’s sprawling beach has emerged at low tide.
In one direction, they face the calm waters of St Aubin’s Bay, ringed by a seaside promenade and punctuated with a tidal island hosting the 16th century Elizabeth Castle.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s unrecognisable’: How being a tax haven has changed Jersey

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Peter Walker; produced by Saskia Collette and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
From hospital wards to bathrooms, where is a transgender person supposed to go after the latest equalities guidance?
Transgender people in Britain are navigating a new reality. In August, new guidance – in the form of a document nearly 350 pages long – was published to help institutions interpret last year’s supreme court ruling on trans rights.
It means, as Amelia outlines to Helen Pidd, that every time she goes to a pub or restaurant, she is terrified about going to the bathroom. As a trans woman, she has used women’s facilities without problems for years; now she’s being told she should use the men’s.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Being trans in Britain in 2026 – podcast

articles.author: Peter Walker and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
Proposal one of many at conference responding to concern voters unaware of party’s policies or what it stands for
The Liberal Democrats say they will tax big tech to finance a new online crime agency, as they try to address concerns that not enough voters know what the party stands for.
The plan, to be announced at the party conference on Monday by the Lib Dems’ home affairs spokesperson, Max Wilkinson, would create a new Online Crime Agency focused on offences including child sexual abuse material, trafficking in drugs and weapons, and deepfake AI-generated pornographic images.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lib Dems propose big tech levy to fund £250m online crime agency

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Funding boost for facilities and fixed dates for trials designed to encourage more survivors to come forward
Specialist courtrooms prioritising cases of rape and other serious sex offences are to be introduced across England and Wales, with campaigners welcoming the move as potentially transformative.
The changes, designed to encourage more survivors to come forward, will include the provision of private entrances and waiting rooms, and facilities equipped for recording evidence in advance and observing sentencing remotely.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Specialist courtrooms to prioritise rape cases in England and Wales

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Bridget Phillipson says Burnham’s past criticisms of US president not an issue as PM prepares to meet Trump at UN
Next month’s budget will be made more difficult by Donald Trump’s war with Iran, one of Andy Burnham’s cabinet ministers has said, while adding she did not expect the prime minister’s previous disparaging comments about the US president to be an issue.
Burnham is expected to meet Trump early next week at the UN general assembly summit in New York, the pair having previously spoken twice by phone since Burnham entered No 10.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK minister warns of impact of Trump’s Iran war on next month’s budget

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Jane Adetoro, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters from Uxbridge were found on 13 May
The deaths of three sisters found in the sea off Brighton beach did not involve any criminality or third-party involvement, police have concluded.
The bodies of Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, from Uxbridge, west London, were found on 13 May. A postmortem conducted that month confirmed all three women died by drowning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Deaths of three women in sea at Brighton had no criminal involvement, police say

articles.description:

articles.title: Andy Burnham faces a weakened Trump – but the president remains unpredictable

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Self-described moderates say Ed Davey’s party offers them a home as Conservatives shift further right
Climbing the party-branded stairs of the Brighton Centre with a Liberal Britain tote bag over his shoulder, Cody Butler looks quite at home at the Liberal Democrats’ annual jamboree.
But asked how he is finding it, the 21-year-old replied: “Odd.” The former Tory activist resigned as chair of the One Nation Conservative Network and left his old party in July, arguing that centrists, remainers and members worried about the climate crisis and conservation were no longer welcome in the party. A week ago, he joined the Lib Dems.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Feeling ‘forced out’ by Badenoch? Lib Dems conference welcomes young Tory defectors

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman
articles.description:
Wife of former PM takes part in designer Edeline Lee’s show inspired by the Greek myth of Sisyphus
Victoria Starmer has taken part in a London fashion week show, in one of her first public appearances since her husband, Keir Starmer, stepped down as prime minister.
Lady Starmer appeared at Sunday’s Edeline Lee show. The London-based, Canadian British designer’s clothes are a favourite of the Princess of Wales, and have also been worn by celebrities including singer Taylor Swift and actor and screenwriter Phoebe Waller-Bridge.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Victoria Starmer models clothes at London fashion week show

articles.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Stark health inequalities in terms of deaths before age of 75, NHS data reveals
Adults with severe mental illness are nearly five times more likely than their peers to die from serious physical diseases before the age of 75, according to research.
The analysis of NHS data by the Rethink Mental Illness charity reveals that people with severe mental health problems die 15-20 years earlier than the wider adult population, largely due to preventable physical conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Adults with severe mental illness die 15 to 20 years earlier from diseases such as cancer

articles.author: Alex Lawson
articles.description:
Unit1 hopes to offer lower cost version of shows such as Abba Voyage, showcasing living and dead artists in any venue
The former chief executive of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s entertainment group has obtained a near-£15m investment for his UK music tech startup that hopes to recreate classic concerts by manifesting musicians as digital avatars.
Unit1 was set up last year by Barney Wragg, an entertainment executive who ran Lord Lloyd-Webber’s Cats-to-Evita empire for five years from late 2011. It has secured the $20m in funding from a group of investors, including tech backer Balderton Capital through its partner Daniel Waterhouse, who made early investments in Spotify.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK startup snares $20m to recreate gigs with ‘hyper-realistic’ digital avatars

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Exclusive: Five gardening teams shortlisted for Royal Horticultural Society’s new Railway Stations in Bloom award
Every year since 1964, towns across the UK have bloomed with hanging baskets and brightly coloured flowerbeds planted by residents.
They wield their trowels in aid of the Royal Horticultural Society’s Britain in Bloom competition, a coveted accolade for the 1,600 communities that enter each year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s transformed the village’: the volunteers greening up Britain’s train stations

articles.author: Rob Evans
articles.description:
Shabana Mahmood is concerned about length and £144m cost of inquiry into intrusive police surveillance
Victims of intrusive police surveillance have accused the government of seeking to cut short the spycops public inquiry that has been examining widespread misconduct committed by undercover officers.
The independent judge-led inquiry is scrutinising how officers, who spied on tens of thousands of political activists over more than four decades, carried out abuses such as deceiving women into sexual relationships and fathering children.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Victims say Home Office attempt to curtail spycops inquiry will result in a ‘cover-up’

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Operator that runs services between London Marylebone and Birmingham is sixth to be nationalised since 2025
Chiltern Railways has become the latest train operator to enter public ownership as the government closes in on its ambition to renationalise all major passenger rail services.
The operator, which runs commuter rail services on the Chiltern mainline between London Marylebone and Birmingham, on Sunday became the sixth to be nationalised under Labour, with the remaining four to follow by the end of 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chiltern Railways enters public ownership in Labour nationalisation push

articles.description:
Josh Babarinde wants to target big tech and crypto billionaires while giving power and cash back to the public
Standing outside Toynbee Hall in the East End of London, Josh Babarinde doesn’t exactly look like a rabble-rouser. But despite the well-cut suit and disarmingly large smile, the president of the Liberal Democrats is, apparently, up for a fight.
“There are big modern giants that are getting in the way of people’s ability to thrive, and it is the job of Liberal Democrats to address that,” says the 33-year-old. “How are we going to do that? Well, first of all, we’ve got to flip the table over and rise up.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Flip the table and rise up’: Lib Dems’ president in combative mood as party gathers in Brighton

articles.author: Richard Partington and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Economies thrown into renewed turmoil as AI debt, Iran war and soaring government bond yields fuel alarm
At the height of the summer, the mood was optimistic in the world’s financial capitals. Powered by the AI revolution, the US stock market had rallied to a fresh all-time high, as investors bet the multitrillion-dollar investment spree would overshadow the hit from the Iran war.
Now the warning lights are flashing red. As the fighting in the Middle East intensifies without clear sign of a resolution, financial markets have been thrown into renewed turmoil. A slowdown looms in the AI arms race, and tinderbox conditions in the market for government debt are fuelling alarm.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Are global stock markets heading for a crash?

articles.author: Yassin El-Moudden
articles.description:
Tory leader claims prime minister is avoiding difficult decisions as she urges him to increase defence spending 
Kemi Badenoch has accused Andy Burnham of “fiddling while Europe is at risk of burning”, as she repeated her call for the prime minister to cut the welfare budget to fund increase spending on defence.
Speaking to the Telegraph, the Tory leader said that “Burnham may be a people pleaser but difficult choices cannot be avoided through dither and delay”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kemi Badenoch accuses Andy Burnham of ‘fiddling while Europe risks burning’

articles.author: Yassin El-Moudden and Daniel Lavelle
articles.description:
Supporters’ club says billionaire should stand down after ‘completely unacceptable’ comments on the UK and empire
Manchester United’s Muslim supporters’ Club (MUMSC) has called for the Premier League side’s co-owner to step down after he made “completely unacceptable” comments during a BBC interview.
Sir Jim Ratcliffe described the UK as being a country “on the slide” from the days when it had “the greatest empire in the world”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Manchester United Muslim fans group calls on co-owner Jim Ratcliffe to quit

articles.author: Julia Kollewe and Amee Joshi
articles.description:
Case highlights severe financial strain on sector across UK as string of university housing schemes fail

Are you having problems with your accommodation provider?

Nearly 70 students in Dundee have been left scrambling to find accommodation for this academic year after the latest in a string of university housing schemes went bust amid severe financial strain on the sector.
Students in the city have been forced to find alternative housing and rapidly move their possessions as term begins this month after the collapse of the owner of Marketgait Apartments, a city centre block.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Students scramble for accommodation after owner goes bust in Dundee

articles.author: Katie Ward
articles.description:
Much of the UK is still officially in drought after its hottest summer on record, but grasslands are slowly recovering their colour
The landscapes of southern England and Wales are slowly regaining their colour after this summer’s extreme heat.
The UK’s hottest summer on record left the south of the country dried out and brown, making the impact of the drought particularly visual.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Before-and-after images show effects of rain in drought-hit England and Wales

articles.author: PA Media
articles.description:
Cole, described as an ‘extraordinary talent’, also appeared in Waiting for God, Tenko and had an extensive theatre career

Stephanie Cole – obituary


The actor Stephanie Cole, best known for roles in Coronation Street, Waiting for God and Open All Hours, has died aged 84.
She also appeared in the prisoner-of-war drama Tenko, A Bit of a Do and Doc Martin.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stephanie Cole, Coronation Street and Open All Hours actor, dies aged 84

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Prof Jim Al-Khalili says he will offer solution to ‘arrow of time’ problem in Royal Institution lectures
Tech billionaires attempting to live for ever are, quite literally, wasting their time, a leading physicist has said.
While some normal people are turning to unregulated peptide injections, cold plunges and supplements in an effort to defy ageing, the ultra-rich are aiming for immortality with even more drastic interventions: the tech chief executive Bryan Johnson has even tried injecting plasma from his 17-year-old son – although he later said he saw no benefit from it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tech billionaires trying to live for ever? That’s a waste of time, says physicist

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Aaron Sharp ; produced by Angus Neale and Bryony Moore ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
Buckingham Palace has issued a rare, and strong, rebuttal to claims made in Earl Spencer’s memoir Swan Song. The book claims that King Charles told Spencer days after Diana’s death and during a heated row over funeral arrangements: ‘Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.’ Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s senior national news editor, Aaron Sharp
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Diana book sparks royal row between King Charles and Earl Spencer - The Latest

articles.author: Frances Ryan and Patrick Butler
articles.description:
Outcry over ‘brazenly discriminatory’ funding practices among NHS care boards and local councils, with wide variations in rules

Opinion: An effective ban on disabled people leaving Britain? We will not settle for it

Disabled people must have a guaranteed right to travel abroad, MPs and peers have said, as further cases emerged of individuals barred from taking holidays as a result of “ridiculous” rules imposed by local NHS care boards and local councils.
Leading figures have called on the government to bring in clear national guidelines to ensure people who require full-time personal assistants (PAs) are not prevented from using funding for their 24/7 support team for breaks and work trips.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disabled people need right to travel abroad, say UK MPs amid ‘ridiculous’ restrictions row

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Digital, culture, media and sport committee expected to hear evidence from BBC bosses and music industry experts
Joe and Jake. Daz Sampson. Electro Velvet. Who could forget them?
Most people, probably. They are some of the many acts who represented the UK at the Eurovision song contest in the last 20 years that have failed to find a place in the country’s cultural pantheon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to answer for its ‘dismal record’ in Eurovision before committee of MPs

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Patients among hundreds who suffered harm at County Durham and Darlington foundation trust’s breast unit
Twenty women had their breasts removed unnecessarily while being treated for cancer at an NHS trust in north-east England.
The County Durham and Darlington foundation trust (CDDFT) told the BBC that the women were among hundreds of patients who came to harm during treatment at its breast unit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Twenty women had breasts removed unnecessarily during NHS cancer care

articles.author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Efra committee calls for emergency legislation enabling government to take public control of the company 
Andy Burnham is under further pressure to take control of ailing Thames Water from a cross-party group of MPs who are calling for ministers to break off talks with the US hedge funds who are effectively running the company.
Adding their voices to demands that the prime minister takes public control of the company, which has debts of £20bn and is being controlled by a group of 100 hedge funds and distressed-debt investors, the MPs said in a report that ministers should consider emergency legislation to take control of its financial affairs to stabilise the company.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MPs urge ministers to break off Thames Water talks with US hedge funds

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
In latest extracts from upcoming memoir, Diana’s brother suggests some in Buckingham Palace were ‘relieved’ at her death
The brother of the late Diana, Princess of Wales, has claimed in published extracts of his new memoir that King Charles sounded “giddily elated – like a lottery winner” in a phone call to him immediately after her death.
Earl Spencer also says he believed Buckingham Palace wanted William and Harry and himself to walk behind Diana’s coffin because the then prince was “adamant” he was going to walk and palace officials feared “members of the public might shout abuse at him”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Charles sounded 'giddily elated' after Diana’s death, claims Earl Spencer

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Rapper won prestigious award as an unsigned artist before breaking UK Top 10 and nurturing artists including KSI
The British rapper Sway, who proved inspirational to a generation of Black British musicians thanks to his independence and frank, dextrous storytelling, has died aged 44.
The news was announced by the Mobo awards, with whom Sway won best hip-hop act in 2005, the first unsigned act to do so. “Proud to have him as part of our history. Our love goes out to his family, loved ones and fans,” the statement read.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sway, Mobo-winning British rapper, dies aged 44

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
This blog is now closed
Andrew Griffith has delivered his speech, and he is now taking questions.
Q: You want the government to pause the making tax digital programme. Is that an admission that the last government got this wrong when it introduced it?
It is an admission that despite [good] intentions, the execution of that has left a lot to be desired.
In fact, coming to parliament from business, I can confess the law that we pass the most often is the law of unintended consequences. And I think making tax digital is a good example of that.
The truth is that Burnham and Miliband ignored the advice they were given – which was that if they were determined to sanction Israel, they should not do so before the Israeli election on 27 October.
It may not be surprising that this was the message from the Israeli foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, when Miliband called him on 11 August to warn sanctions were imminent. ‘He said postpone it until after the elections,’ a diplomatic source confirms. It was also the message the Israeli embassy in London – and its new chargé d’affaires Chris Cantor – was relaying to the Foreign Office. ‘Their message was clear: why do it now? Wait until after the elections, because something might change,’ a senior Labour figure says.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Khan addresses Polanski in Urdu at London assembly, mocking Green leader’s byelection video – as it happened

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
From ‘there were three of us in this marriage’ to ‘recollections may vary’, a lot can be conveyed with a carefully worded phrase
As denials go, King Charles’s response to Earl Spencer’s allegations that Charles said after Diana’s death, “We’ll forget her soon enough”, was a masterclass in the diplomatic royal rebuke.
Rarely has Buckingham Palace responded to claims in countless books on royalty. But it was straight out of the block on this one.

articles.title: Charles’s rebuttal of Earl Spencer’s claim about Diana offers rare glimpse into palace thinking

articles.author: Bethan McKernan Wales correspondent
articles.description:
Community groups and schools work with Wales’s folk arts organisation to set  stories of the area’s people to music
Growing up in Wales, Liz Puleston-Jones was familiar with the country’s rich heritage of storytelling and traditional music, but none of it ever seemed to have much of a connection to her life in Swansea.
Researching the history of the area as part of Cân y Cymoedd (When Valleys Sing), a project in nearby Port Talbot, she came across the story of Isabel Thomas, a 14-year-old girl in the 1940s who left school and lied about her age to work in a tin plate works to support her family.
